title: Kunneth isomorphism for quasi-coherent cohomology over a field
statement: Let k be a field [def-weil-field], let X and Y be schemes over k [def-pc-scheme], and let F and G be quasi-coherent modules on X and Y [pqf-def-coherent]. If X and Y are quasi-compact and have affine diagonals, then for every integer n >= 0 the canonical cup-product map H^n(X \times_{\operatorname{Spec}(k)} Y, \operatorname{pr}_1^*F \otimes_{\mathcal O_{X \times_{\operatorname{Spec}(k)} Y}} \operatorname{pr}_2^*G) \cong \bigoplus_{p+q=n} H^p(X,F) \otimes_k H^q(Y,G) is an isomorphism. The canonical map is obtained by pulling cohomology classes back along the two projections and applying the cup product, and is functorial for pullback along morphisms of schemes over k.

source.place: Varieties, Lemma varieties-lemma-kunneth (the Kunneth lemma used in Tag 0BED)

proof.text: Choose finite affine covers U of X and V of Y. Their product cover W by U_i x_{Spec(k)} V_j is finite and affine: products of affine opens are affine by lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra. By lem-sc-picard-affine-diagonal-intersections the intersection of two affine opens of X (resp. Y) is affine, so by induction on the number of members every finite intersection U_{i_0..i_p} (resp. V_{j_0..j_p}) is affine, and W_{(i_0j_0)..(i_pj_p)} = U_{i_0..i_p} x_k V_{j_0..j_p} is affine. Refinement pullbacks (W refines pr_1^{-1}U and pr_2^{-1}V) and the signed Cech cup construction give the map Tot(Cech(U,F) tensor_k Cech(V,G)) \to Cech(W,pr_1^*F tensor pr_2^*G).

source.place: Varieties, Lemma varieties-lemma-kunneth, proof before equation equation-kunneth-on-cech

proof.text: The field-linear algebra Kunneth lemma lem-sc-qcoh-cech-total-tensor-iso identifies the direct sum of tensor products of the two Cech cohomologies with the cohomology of the total tensor complex, by the map [a] tensor [b] \mapsto [a tensor b].

The Cech comparison theorem lem-sc-cech-comparison-map-iso-affine, together with its naturality, identifies those Cech cohomology groups with H^p(X,F), H^q(Y,G), and H^n(X x_k Y,pr_1^*F tensor pr_2^*G). The Cech cup compatibility lemma identifies the resulting map with pullback along the projections followed by the sheaf cup product.

source.place: Varieties, Lemma varieties-lemma-kunneth, proof after equation equation-kunneth-on-cech

proof.text: For a short exact sequence 0 \to F \to F' \to F'' \to 0 of quasi-coherent modules, sections on every affine intersection U_{i_0..i_p} are exact by pqf-lem-affine-vanishing (Tag 01XB), and tensoring the resulting short exact sequence of k-vector spaces with any k-vector space is exact (k is a field). On the affine W_{(i_0j_0)..(i_pj_p)} = U_{i_0..i_p} x_k V_{j_0..j_p} the sections of pr_1^*F tensor pr_2^*G are F(U_{i_0..i_p}) tensor_k G(V_{j_0..j_p}), naturally in F and G, by lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections (sections of a pullback on affines are the base change of the sections), lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra and lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-tensor-product-affine-sections. Thus the Cech complexes and their tensor-total complexes form short exact sequences of complexes, and the map of Step 1 is a map of short exact sequences. The long exact cohomology sequences and the five lemma give a 2-out-of-3 principle: if the map of Step 1 is a quasi-isomorphism for two of F, F', F'' (with G fixed), it is one for the third; by Steps 2 and 3 this is the Kunneth assertion. The same holds in the variable G.

proof.text: Finite cohomological dimension on X and the universal-delta-functor embedding lemma give an induction on d(F)=max{d | H^d(X,F) != 0}: embed F into F' with higher cohomology zero, let F'' be the cokernel, and use the 2-out-of-3 principle because d(F'')<d(F). Repeating in Y reduces to the case where F and G have cohomology only in degree zero.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Tags 01XI and 0BDY, as invoked in Tag 0BED Varieties Lemma varieties-lemma-kunneth

proof.text: Degree-zero case: H^p(X,F)=0 and H^q(Y,G)=0 for p,q>0. Put H = pr_1^*F tensor pr_2^*G. For every affine open V of Y, pr_2^{-1}(V) = X x_k V, and the cover U_V = (U_i x_k V) of X x_k V has affine finite intersections U_{i_0..i_p} x_k V by Step 1 and lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra. By lem-sc-cech-comparison-map-iso-affine, H^q(X x_k V, H) is the cohomology of Cech(U_V,H), and as in Step 4 (lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections, lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-tensor-product-affine-sections) Cech(U_V,H) = Cech(U,F) tensor_k G(V); tensoring over the field k is exact, so H^q(X x_k V,H) = H^q(Cech(U,F)) tensor_k G(V) = H^q(X,F) tensor_k G(V) (lem-sc-cech-comparison-map-iso-affine on X), which is 0 for q>0 and Gamma(X,F) tensor_k G(V) for q=0. By lem-weil-pbc-higher-direct-image-presheaf, R^q pr_{2,*}H is the sheaf associated to V \mapsto H^q(X x_k V,H), with stalks the colimits of these groups over neighbourhoods of a point; the affine opens are cofinal among these, so R^q pr_{2,*}H = 0 for q>0. For q=0, choose a k-basis (e_s) of Gamma(X,F); the map from the direct sum of copies of G indexed by s to pr_{2,*}H, sending t in G(V) at index s to pr_1^*e_s tensor pr_2^*t, is on every affine V the map from the direct sum of the G(V) (lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-cohomology-direct-sum with p=0 on the affine, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated, V) to Gamma(X,F) tensor_k G(V), an isomorphism; isomorphisms on a basis of opens give isomorphisms on stalks, so pr_{2,*}H = Gamma(X,F) tensor_k G.

source.place: Varieties, Lemma varieties-lemma-kunneth, degree-zero case after the induction

proof.text: The diagonal of Y is affine, hence quasi-compact, so Y is quasi-compact and quasi-separated; by lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-cohomology-direct-sum, H^p(Y, Gamma(X,F) tensor_k G) is the direct sum of copies of H^p(Y,G), which is 0 for p>0, and its global sections are Gamma(X,F) tensor_k Gamma(Y,G). With Step 6, H^p(Y,R^q pr_{2,*}H) = 0 for all q >= 0 and p > 0, so by lem-pc-leray-degenerate-sections (2) the edge map H^q(X x_k Y,H) \to Gamma(Y,R^q pr_{2,*}H) is an isomorphism for every q: the product cohomology is zero above degree zero and in degree zero is Gamma(X,F) tensor_k Gamma(Y,G). Both sides of the Kunneth map are thus concentrated in degree zero, where the canonical map is s tensor t \mapsto pr_1^*s . pr_2^*t (lem-sc-picard-cech-cup-pullback-compat in degree 0), which is the isomorphism just obtained. With Steps 4 and 5 this proves the Kunneth isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0BED, final degree-zero paragraph and omitted cup-product verification

proof.text: Functoriality. Let u:X'\to X and v:Y'\to Y be morphisms of schemes over k and w = u x_k v : X' x_k Y' \to X x_k Y, so that pr_1 o w = u o pr_1' and pr_2 o w = v o pr_2' (def-pc-fibre-product); identify w^*(pr_1^*F tensor pr_2^*G) with pr_1'^*u^*F tensor pr_2'^*v^*G by lem-pc-module-pullback-identity-composition and lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-tensor. The claim is w^*(pr_1^*a cup pr_2^*b) = pr_1'^*u^*a cup pr_2'^*v^*b for a in H^p(X,F), b in H^q(Y,G). With U, V, W as in Step 1, a = c_U(alpha) and b = c_V(beta) for Cech cocycles alpha, beta (lem-sc-cech-comparison-map-iso-affine). Use the covers u^{-1}U, v^{-1}V and W' = w^{-1}W, which refines pr_1'^{-1}u^{-1}U and pr_2'^{-1}v^{-1}V by (i,j) \mapsto i, j since w^{-1}(U_i x V_j) is contained in w^{-1}pr_1^{-1}U_i = pr_1'^{-1}u^{-1}U_i. By lem-sc-picard-cech-cup-pullback-compat (a), each pullback in the claim is computed by the refinement cochain map, whose components are pullbacks of sections; by lem-pc-module-pullback-identity-composition the cochains obtained from alpha along w after pr_1 and along pr_1' after u coincide (both are pullback of the components along pr_1 o w = u o pr_1'), and likewise for beta. By lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-tensor (w^*(s tensor t) = w^*s tensor w^*t) the refinement cochain map along w sends the signed Cech cup product of two cochains to the cup product of their images. By lem-sc-picard-cech-cup-pullback-compat (b) the Cech cup products induce the sheaf cup products on X x_k Y and on X' x_k Y'. Hence both sides of the claim are c_{W'} of the same cochain, which proves the functoriality clause.
